title: Sunny Watches the Firefly Dance | Bedtime Story
description: Sonny the little quokka sits perfectly still in a moonlit clearing and watches dozens of fireflies blink in slow, gentle rhythms — until her own eyes begin to blink along and grow too heavy to open. A dreamy bedtime story from Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales, ideal for easing little ones into sleep.
narration:
The evening had settled softly over the bush, and the sky above the gum trees was a deep, velvety blue. Sonny the little quokka followed the sound of the crickets to a small clearing she had never visited at night before.

She stepped into the clearing — and gasped the tiniest gasp.

Fireflies. Dozens and dozens of them, drifting and hovering through the warm night air. Each one carried a tiny lantern, and the lanterns blinked on and off, on and off, in the most gentle, dreamy rhythm. Blink. Pause. Blink. Pause. Blink.

Sunny sat down right where she was, in the soft grass at the edge of the clearing, and she went completely still. She didn't want to disturb a single one.

The fireflies drifted like slow sparks. Some were high up near the tree branches. Some floated low over the grass. Their lights were soft yellow-green, and they pulsed slowly, like tiny heartbeats.

Sunny watched them for a long, long time.

And after a while, without even meaning to, she started to blink along with them. Blink... pause... blink... pause... blink.

Her blinks grew slower. And slower. And after each one, her eyelids felt just a little bit heavier, like they were weighted with starlight.

Blink.

Pause.

Blink...

The fireflies danced on in the dark, their quiet lights filling the whole clearing with something like magic. And Sunny, curled in the soft grass, drifted gently away into the deepest, most peaceful sleep.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, fireflies. Goodnight, little one.
